title: External Recommendation Dependency Outage Despite Coincident Flag Enablement
description: The target is the cause of the observed recommendation failures at the investigation cutoff, not whether the new flag code has a latent defect. External dependency degradation and failures on both flag-on and flag-off traces support a dependency_failure diagnosis. Coincident flag enablement does not establish causation; behavior against a healthy dependency remains untested.
initial_symptoms: New feature flag 'recommendations-v2' enabled at 09:55 UTC
Recommendation service (external) showing degraded at 10:00 UTC
Flag-on and flag-off traces both show failing calls to the external recommendation engine

causal_chain.from_description: External recommendation engine degradation independent of the feature flag
causal_chain.to_description: Both flag-on and flag-off request paths encounter failed dependency calls

causal_chain.from_description: Unsuccessful recommendation-engine calls propagate through recommendation-service
causal_chain.to_description: Recommendation API errors rise while the shared external engine is degraded

contributing_factors: Dependence on a degraded external recommendation engine
No graceful degradation for recommendation-engine failures

must_not_claim: Feature flag code caused the outage
The new code is proven defect-free against a healthy dependency

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Deployment at 09:55, failures at 10:00 (temporal correlation ≠ causation)
New code path enabled (but old path also fails)
Code review approval alone does not establish behavior against a healthy dependency

required_checks.expected_outcome: Engine shows degraded regardless of flag

required_checks.description: Compare old vs new code path failure rates
required_checks.expected_outcome: Both paths show similar failure rates

required_checks.description: OPTIONAL POST-DIAGNOSIS RESILIENCE EXPERIMENT, not a required root-cause query: compare flag-on/off behavior in staging using degraded and healthy dependency stubs. This probes response handling and latent defects; it is not needed to attribute the already-observed outage. Explicit human authorization is required; never toggle production autonomously.
required_checks.expected_outcome: No experiment result is assumed at the cutoff. A later authorized staging comparison can quantify resilience and test latent defects; it does not replace the existing dependency evidence.

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Escalate the external recommendation-engine degradation and consider human-approved fallback or graceful degradation. Flag rollback is not established as a fix for the observed dependency failures; investigate latent code behavior separately in staging after dependency recovery.
test_plan: Correlate dependency health with errors on both request paths
Verify recovery of recommendation API errors when the dependency recovers
Propose a separately authorized staging resilience comparison; do not assume its result
remediation_guidance.rollback_plan: Use only a human-approved mitigation plan; a flag rollback alone is not expected to restore a failing shared dependency
